Prompt¶

Conduct a reproducible, multi-knowledge-graph integrative study of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) to generate a comprehensive, evidence-backed map of its molecular biology, genetics, immunology, neuropathology, clinical manifestations, epidemiology, and therapeutic landscape. Follow the /okn-bioanalysis workflow and produce the final report using /okn-report-style.

  1. Characterize MS and its subtypes (CIS, RRMS, SPMS, PPMS, PRMS where historical), including synonyms, ontology mappings and crosswalks, and differences in definitions, criteria and staging.
  2. Integrate across all relevant mcp-okn KGs: harmonize identifiers, use cross-graph joins, and document which KGs contributed to each finding.
  3. Build the molecular profile organized by entity type — protein-coding genes, ncRNAs (kept separate), variants, proteins/complexes, pathways/gene sets, biological processes, molecular functions and upstream regulators — focusing on adaptive and innate immunity, T/B-cell activation, HLA/MHC, cytokine/chemokine signalling, microglia, astrocytes, de/remyelination, oligodendrocytes, axonal degeneration, neuroinflammation, BBB, mitochondria, oxidative stress and complement; rank genes, variants and pathways by evidence.
  4. Characterize disease-associated activity: record tissue, region, compartment, cell type, subtype, stage, direction, context and datasets; highlight consistently dysregulated genes.
  5. Map the therapeutic landscape (IFN-β, glatiramer, S1P modulators, natalizumab, ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, alemtuzumab, cladribine, DMF, BTK inhibitors) with targets, pathways and mechanism of action; identify repurposing opportunities.
  6. Clinical features and biomarkers: phenotypes, MRI, CSF, blood, NfL, oligoclonal bands, genetic risk, progression and response markers, ranked.
  7. Epidemiology: prevalence and incidence by region, linked to age, sex, ancestry, latitude, vitamin D, EBV, smoking, obesity, socioeconomic factors and SDoH; report statistical correlations and provide prevalence/incidence maps.
  8. For every relationship record the KG(s), relationship type, confidence/effect size and evidence type (curated, genetic association, differential activity, pathway membership, protein interaction, clinical association, literature), keeping categories separate rather than merged.
  9. Rank by cross-source agreement; identify conflicts, gaps, ontology mismatches and under-researched areas; distinguish established from emerging mechanisms.

Notes¶

12 OKN KGs integrated on a ubergraph-harmonised MS anchor (MONDO_0005301 = DOID:2377 = UMLS C0026769). Evidence categories kept separate; tiers A-D by cross-source agreement. q15, q23 and q34 are superseded and unused. Natural Earth (GDP, boundaries) is an external covariate.

Re-running this study¶

Every query cell loads the rows the session logged (data/), so the notebook runs offline and shows the original results. To rerun the study from scratch, uncomment # RERUN = True in the next cell and run all cells (or start Jupyter with OKN_RERUN=1): every query is then re-executed live against the OKN federation. Or run the last cell (verify_all()) to compare each query's live row count with the logged one. A changed count usually means the knowledge graph was redeployed since the study ran, not that the analysis is wrong.

In [1]:
import os

import pandas as pd

from okn_sparql import run_query, verify_all

# By default (RERUN = False) every query cell loads the rows logged during the
# session from data/, so the notebook runs offline and shows the original results.
# Starting Jupyter with OKN_RERUN=1 sets RERUN = True without editing the notebook.
RERUN = os.environ.get("OKN_RERUN", "") == "1"

# To rerun the study from scratch, uncomment the next line and run all cells:
# every query is then re-executed live against the OKN federation.
# RERUN = True

q01 — q01 ubergraph: lookup of the MS disease term¶

2026-11-19T09:26:35+00:00 · ubergraph · 6 rows logged

SPARQL (17 lines) 
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX oio: <http://www.geneontology.org/formats/oboInOwl#>
SELECT DISTINCT ?term ?label ?matched_on ?matched_text WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/ubergraph> {
    { VALUES ?lit { "multiple sclerosis" "multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple sclerosis" "Multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple Sclerosis" "Multiple Sclerosis"@en } ?term rdfs:label ?lit . BIND("label" AS ?matched_on) }
    UNION
    { VALUES ?lit { "multiple sclerosis" "multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple sclerosis" "Multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple Sclerosis" "Multiple Sclerosis"@en } ?term oio:hasExactSynonym ?lit . BIND("exact_synonym" AS ?matched_on) }
    UNION
    { VALUES ?lit { "multiple sclerosis" "multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple sclerosis" "Multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple Sclerosis" "Multiple Sclerosis"@en } ?term oio:hasRelatedSynonym ?lit . BIND("related_synonym" AS ?matched_on) }
    UNION
    { VALUES ?lit { "multiple sclerosis" "multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple sclerosis" "Multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple Sclerosis" "Multiple Sclerosis"@en } ?term oio:hasNarrowSynonym ?lit . BIND("narrow_synonym" AS ?matched_on) }
    UNION
    { VALUES ?lit { "multiple sclerosis" "multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple sclerosis" "Multiple sclerosis"@en "Multiple Sclerosis" "Multiple Sclerosis"@en } ?term oio:hasBroadSynonym ?lit . BIND("broad_synonym" AS ?matched_on) }
    OPTIONAL { ?term rdfs:label ?label }
  }
  BIND(STR(?lit) AS ?matched_text)
} LIMIT 25

q08 — q08 spoke-okn: MS node by label¶

2026-11-19T09:27:05+00:00 · spoke-okn · 2 rows logged

SPARQL (11 lines) 
PREFIX biolink: <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX kg: <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-okn/schema/>
SELECT ?d ?label (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STR(?see); separator="|") AS ?seeAlso) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STR(?mesh); separator="|") AS ?meshList) WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-okn> {
    ?d a biolink:Disease ; rdfs:label ?label .
    FILTER(CONTAINS(LCASE(STR(?label)), "sclerosis") || CONTAINS(LCASE(STR(?label)), "demyelinat"))
    OPTIONAL { ?d rdfs:seeAlso ?see }
    OPTIONAL { ?d kg:mesh_list ?mesh }
  }
} GROUP BY ?d ?label

SPARQL (14 lines) 
PREFIX kg: <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-okn/schema/>
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
SELECT ?rel ?compound ?name ?phase ?source ?act WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-okn> {

    OPTIONAL { ?compound rdfs:label ?name }
    OPTIONAL { ?st kg:phase ?phase }
    OPTIONAL { ?st dcterms:source ?source }
    OPTIONAL { ?st kg:act_sources ?act }
  }
}

PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX obo: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/>
PREFIX biolink_model: <https://biolink.github.io/biolink-model/>
SELECT ?d ?p ?ent ?entlabel (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STR(?etype); separator="|") AS ?etypes) WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-okn> { <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/DOID_2377> a <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/Disease> . }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/ubergraph> { ?msroot <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#exactMatch> <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/DOID_2377> . ?mondo rdfs:subClassOf* ?msroot . }
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> {
    ?d <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#exactMatch> ?mondo .
    VALUES ?p { biolink_model:associated_with obo:NCIT_C41184 obo:RO_0002410 <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/bto#related_to> obo:RO_0003308 }
    ?ent ?p ?d .
    OPTIONAL { ?ent rdfs:label ?entlabel } OPTIONAL { ?ent a ?etype }
  }
} GROUP BY ?d ?p ?ent ?entlabel

q22 — q22 prokn: drug -> target for MS-indicated compounds¶

2026-11-19T09:33:41+00:00 · prokn · 235 rows logged

SPARQL (15 lines) 
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX obo: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?drug (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?lab; separator="|") AS ?labels) (MAX(?ph) AS ?max_phase) ?target (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?tlab; separator="|") AS ?target_labels) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STR(?action); separator="|") AS ?actions) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STR(?mech); separator="|") AS ?mechanisms) WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/prokn> {
    VALUES ?d { <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/DOID_2377> <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/DOID_2378> <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/DOID_0050783> <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/?term=D009103> }
    ?st rdf:object ?d ; rdf:predicate obo:NCIT_C41184 ; rdf:subject ?drug .
    OPTIONAL { ?st <https://w3id.org/reproduceme#Phase> ?ph }
    OPTIONAL { ?drug rdfs:label ?lab }
    OPTIONAL { ?ts rdf:subject ?drug ; rdf:predicate <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/directly_physically_interacts_with> ; rdf:object ?target .
               OPTIONAL { ?target rdfs:label ?tlab }
               OPTIONAL { ?ts <http://purl.allotrope.org/ontologies/result#AFR_0003142> ?action }
               OPTIONAL { ?ts <http://snomed.info/id/257544000> ?mech } }
  }
} GROUP BY ?drug ?target

SPARQL (9 lines) 
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT (REPLACE(STR(?g),"^.*/","") AS ?entrez) (SAMPLE(?sym) AS ?s) (MAX(?w) AS ?maxw) WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/digcfdekg> {
    ?st rdf:object <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MONDO_0005301> ; rdf:predicate <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/digcfdekg/schema/geneToTrait> ; rdf:subject ?g ; <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/digcfdekg/schema/weight> ?w .
    OPTIONAL { ?g rdfs:label ?sym }
    FILTER(REPLACE(STR(?g),"^.*/","") > "960")
  }
} GROUP BY ?g

q50 — q50 gene-expression-atlas-okn + spoke-okn: Entrez -> symbol¶

2026-11-19T09:46:04+00:00 · gene-expression-atlas-okn, spoke-okn · 683 rows logged

SPARQL (10 lines) 
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT DISTINCT (REPLACE(STR(?g),"^.*/","") AS ?entrez) ?symbol WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/gene-expression-atlas-okn> {
    VALUES ?assay { <http://purl.org/okn/wobd/assay/E-GEOD-66573-g1_g2> <http://purl.org/okn/wobd/assay/E-GEOD-77598-g2_g1> <http://purl.org/okn/wobd/assay/E-MTAB-2973-g3_g2> <http://purl.org/okn/wobd/assay/E-MTAB-69-g3_g1> <http://purl.org/okn/wobd/assay/E-GEOD-26104-g7_g3> <http://purl.org/okn/wobd/assay/E-GEOD-14386-g2_g1> }
    ?x <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/subject> ?assay ; <https://w3id.org/biolink/vocab/object> ?g0 ; <http://purl.org/okn/wobd/log2fc> ?l ; <http://purl.org/okn/wobd/adj_p_value> ?p .
    FILTER(?p <= 0.05 && ABS(?l) >= 1)
  }
  BIND(IRI(CONCAT("http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/", REPLACE(STR(?g0),"^.*/",""))) AS ?g)
  GRAPH <https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/spoke-okn> { ?g rdfs:label ?symbol }
}

Analysis¶

Question and approach¶

Question. What does the OKN federation, taken as a whole, say about multiple sclerosis (its subtypes, genes and pathways, disease-associated expression, therapies, clinical features and biomarkers, and epidemiology), and where do the graphs agree, conflict or fall silent?

Why it matters. Evidence on MS is spread across curated databases, genetic association studies, expression atlases, drug resources, EHR co-occurrence and literature mining. Putting it on one disease anchor shows which mechanisms several independent kinds of evidence support, which therapies act on genetically supported targets, and where the graphs have gaps or errors.

Approach. The queries above anchor MS in ubergraph (MONDO_0005301 = DOID:2377 = UMLS C0026769) and pull evidence from 12 knowledge graphs on that anchor. The cells below map identifiers across graphs, build a gene evidence matrix that keeps evidence categories separate and ranks genes by cross-source agreement, profile expression, therapeutics, phenotypes and biomarkers, and epidemiology, and finish with enrichment, a protein-interaction network and a mechanistic map. The exact joins, thresholds and tier rules are in the specification that follows.

Replicator specification¶

Study. Integrative multi-KG map of multiple sclerosis (MS-2026-11-19). Model claude-opus-5-5. OKN federated SPARQL (FRINK). Framing: hypothesis generation from curated, genetic, text-mined and observational associations; no causal or clinical inference.

Query map (logical name → logged query). The data["qNN"] frames are mapped by QMAP in the setup cell. q15 and q34 are superseded (BIND-scoping error in a UNION; wrong counts) and q23 is superseded by q24. These three are kept in the log for transparency but used nowhere.

Disease anchor and subtypes (ubergraph, q01–q07). MONDO_0005301 and its rdfs:subClassOf* closure: RRMS MONDO_0005314, SPMS MONDO_0000450, PPMS MONDO_0000451, PRMS MONDO_0000452, chronic progressive MONDO_0005284, Marburg MONDO_0016429, paediatric MONDO_0018784. Cross-references come from skos:exactMatch + oboInOwl:hasDbXref (q07). There is no exact CIS term.

Joins.

  • spoke-okn: DOID_2377 via ubergraph exactMatch (q08–q14); genes on Entrez; countries on ISO3.
  • rdkg: MONDO IRIs directly plus rdkg grouped nodes (q16–q18).
  • prokn: DOID_2377 / DOID_2378 / DOID_0050783 and MeSH D009103 nodes (q19–q22).
  • digcfdekg: MONDO_0005301 geneToTrait PIGEAN maxw (q24 + tails q47/q48 for the 1,000-row cap).
  • oard-kg: reified associations; the HP term may sit on biolink:subject OR biolink:object (UNION); kept LOR ≥ 1.5 and ≥ 20 co-occurring patients (q25).
  • biomarkerkg: MONDO_0005301 (q26, q27).
  • gene-expression-atlas-okn: MONDO assays (q28); DE at adj p ≤ 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 1 (q29, q30); Entrez→symbol via spoke-okn (q50).
  • wikidata: Q8277 via P699 "DOID:2377" (q41); statements (q39); P625 coordinates on ISO3 P298 (q40).
  • biohealth: ubergraph hasDbXref "UMLS:C0026769" → biohealth node IRI (q42, q43).
  • nde: datasets per MONDO subtype (q44).
  • nestkg: PPI among the signature symbols via prokn proteins (q45, q46 in two halves for the row cap).
  • UniProt→symbol for prokn targets comes from q49.

Gene evidence matrix (analysis.evidence_matrix). Seven counted sources: spoke-okn, rdkg (curated); digcfdekg, wikidata P2293 (genetic); biomarkerkg analyte GID; GXA disease contrasts (E-GEOD-66573, E-GEOD-77598, E-MTAB-2973, E-MTAB-69); prokn drug→target. IFN-β contrasts (E-GEOD-26104, E-GEOD-14386) are reported separately and never counted.

  • Tiers. A = ≥ 4 sources, or ≥ 3 including curated + genetic. B = 3 sources, or 2 that are curated + genetic. C = other 2-source genes. D = 1 source.
  • Score. n_sources + 0.25·log1p(PPI degree) + 0.05·min(PIGEAN, 10).
  • ncRNA. Symbols matching LINC/MIR/SNHG/SNOR/RMRP/-AS are flagged and listed separately.
  • Analyst mappings. ChEMBL complex targets → member genes; biomarkerkg analyte names (APOA1, SPHK1, SPHK2, RMRP); prokn target labels for CD52, ERVW-1 and TNFSF13B.

Enrichment.

  • Foreground: spoke-okn ∪ rdkg genes ∪ digcfdekg PIGEAN ≥ 3 (345 symbols). Of these, 220 resolve to prokn genes; 216 carry GO BP and 183 carry Reactome annotation.
  • Backgrounds: prokn genes with direct GO BP biolink:actively_involved_in annotation (N = 7,663), excluding NegativePropertyAssertion, or with Reactome R-HSA participates_in annotation (N = 6,032).
  • Tested: terms with k ≥ 5 (GO, 167 terms) or k ≥ 6 (Reactome, 60 pathways).
  • Statistics: hypergeometric upper tail with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR.

Epidemiology.

  • Prevalence: IHME 2019 percent × 1,000 = per 100,000 (q13).
  • Deaths: WHO GHE deaths / population × 10⁵ (q14). The mort100k field is not used because it is mislabeled.
  • Statistics: Spearman correlations; partial ρ(latitude, prevalence | GDP) from rank residuals; Kruskal–Wallis across continents.
  • GDP per capita and polygons: Natural Earth (ne_countries.geojson in the study data/), an external covariate.

Verified quantities.

  • Evidence matrix: 1,748 genes; tiers A/B/C/D = 55/107/96/1,490.
  • Enrichment: GO 159/167 and Reactome 58/60 terms at FDR < 0.05.
  • Prevalence: ρ(|lat|) = 0.836 (n = 200); ρ(GDP) = 0.698 (n = 165); partial ρ = 0.743.
  • Drugs: prokn has 204 MS-indicated compounds acting on 71 target genes.

Limitations. Associations only. 1,000-row cache cap (tails recovered). Direct, non-propagated GO annotations. GXA sex confounding (Y-chromosome genes removed). oard-kg cohort noise. biohealth predications lack effect sizes. No incidence data, sub-national prevalence or SDoH edges for MS.

§3 Design — identifier crosswalk and per-KG contributions¶

Before combining graphs, confirm they name the same disease: map MS and its subtypes across identifier schemes, and count what each graph contributes.

In [53]:
# Figure 1 — subtype identifier crosswalk (ubergraph) + per-KG contribution
xr = Q["xrefs"].copy()
xr["scheme"] = xr.xref.str.split(":").str[0].replace({"MESH": "MeSH", "SCTID": "SNOMED CT", "icd11.foundation": "ICD-11",
                                                     "ICD10CM": "ICD-10-CM", "ICD10WHO": "ICD-10", "MEDGEN": "MedGen", "ICD9": "ICD-9"})

§5.2 Gene evidence matrix and confidence tiers¶

Rank genes by how many independent sources agree, keeping curated, genetic, expression, biomarker and drug-target evidence separate (tiers A–D in the specification).

In [54]:

m.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/gene_evidence_matrix.csv", index=False)

STATS.update({"n_genes": len(m), "tier_A": int(tiers.A), "tier_B": int(tiers.B), "tier_C": int(tiers.C), "tier_D": int(tiers.D)})
SRC_LABEL = {"spoke_okn": "spoke-okn (curated)", "rdkg": "rdkg (curated)", "digcfdekg": "digcfdekg (GWAS/PIGEAN)",

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(15, 7.5))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, width_ratios=[1, 1.6], height_ratios=[1, 1])

§5.3 Disease-associated and IFN-β-induced expression¶

Which genes change in MS blood, cells and CSF, and which change under IFN-β treatment? Only genes that recur across contrasts are trusted.

In [55]:
# Figure 3 — disease-associated expression (gene-expression-atlas-okn): recurrent DE genes across contrasts
sym = A.gene_symbol_map(Q)
gx = A.gxa_de_table(Q, sym)
gx.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/gxa_differential_expression.csv", index=False)
cnt = Q["gxa_counts"].copy(); STATS["gxa_contrasts_with_de"] = int(((cnt.n_up + cnt.n_down) > 0).sum())
dis = gx[(gx.kind == "disease") & ~gx.sex_chrom_Y]
rec = dis.groupby("symbol").agg(n_contrasts=("a", "nunique"), n_up=("direction", lambda s: (s == "up").sum()),
                                n_down=("direction", lambda s: (s == "down").sum())).reset_index()
rec["consistent"] = (rec.n_up == 0) | (rec.n_down == 0)
rec = rec.sort_values(["n_contrasts", "symbol"], ascending=[False, True])
rec.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/gxa_recurrent_genes.csv", index=False)
STATS.update({"gxa_rec2": int((rec.n_contrasts >= 2).sum()), "gxa_rec2_consistent": int(((rec.n_contrasts >= 2) & rec.consistent).sum()),
              "gxa_de_genes": int(gx.entrez.nunique()), "gxa_y_genes": int(gx[gx.sex_chrom_Y].symbol.nunique())})
ifn = gx[gx.kind == "treatment"]
# rows: recurrent disease genes (>=2 contrasts) + top IFN-response genes also DE in disease
r2 = rec[rec.n_contrasts >= 2].symbol.tolist()
ifn_top = (ifn.groupby("symbol").l2fc.max().sort_values(ascending=False).head(14).index.tolist())
rows = list(dict.fromkeys(r2 + ifn_top))
cols = list(A.GXA_DISEASE) + list(A.GXA_TREAT)
colnames = ["RRMS blood\n66573", "MS mono\n77598", "MS blood\nMTAB-2973", "MS CSF\nMTAB-69", "IFNβ PBMC\n26104", "IFNβ blood\n14386"]
piv = gx[gx.symbol.isin(rows)].pivot_table(index="symbol", columns="a", values="l2fc", aggfunc="first").reindex(index=rows, columns=cols)
STATS["fig4_rows"] = len(rows)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, max(6, 0.3 * len(rows) + 1.5)))
notes = [f"{int(rec.set_index('symbol').n_contrasts.get(s, 0))} dis." for s in rows]
im = F.diverging_heatmap(ax, piv.values, rows, colnames, row_notes=notes, vmax=3.0, na="·", rotate_x=False)
ax.axvline(3.5, color="k", lw=1.2)
cb = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.12); cb.set_label("log2 fold-change")
F.panel_title(ax, "", "Recurrent MS-dysregulated genes and IFN-β response genes")
F.finalize(fig, 3, "figures/fig3_expression_heatmap.png")

§5.4 Therapeutic landscape¶

Which graphs record the approved MS therapies, what do they target, and do those targets have genetic support?

In [56]:
# Figure 4 — therapeutic landscape: requested DMT classes across KGs, prokn phase profile, target genetic support
tg = A.prokn_targets(Q); tg.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/prokn_drug_targets.csv", index=False)
dlong, dagg = A.drug_table(Q)
dagg.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/drug_landscape.csv", index=False)
rd_txt = dlong[dlong.kg == "rdkg"].drug.str.lower().tolist()
wd_txt = dlong[dlong.kg == "wikidata"].drug.str.lower().tolist()
pk_txt = (Q["prokn_indications"].label.astype(str).str.lower().tolist()
          + Q["prokn_targets"].labels.astype(str).str.lower().tolist())  # q22 = targets of the same MS-indicated set
DMT_ROWS = [("Interferon-β", ["interferon beta", "interferon β", "rebif", "beta-interferon", "peginterferon"]),
            ("Glatiramer acetate", ["glatiramer", "copaxone"]), ("Fingolimod", ["fingolimod", "fty720"]),
            ("Siponimod", ["siponimod"]), ("Ozanimod", ["ozanimod"]), ("Ponesimod", ["ponesimod"]),
            ("Natalizumab", ["natalizumab", "tysabri"]), ("Ocrelizumab", ["ocrelizumab"]), ("Ofatumumab", ["ofatumumab"]),
            ("Ublituximab", ["ublituximab"]), ("Alemtuzumab", ["alemtuzumab"]), ("Cladribine", ["cladribine"]),
            ("Fumarates (DMF/DRF/MMF)", ["dimethyl fumarate", "diroximel", "monomethyl fumarate", "bg00012"]),
            ("Teriflunomide", ["teriflunomide"]), ("Mitoxantrone", ["mitoxantrone"]),
            ("BTK inhibitors", ["tolebrutinib", "evobrutinib", "fenebrutinib", "remibrutinib"])]
hit = lambda txts, keys: any(k in t for t in txts for k in keys)
rows = []
for name, keys in DMT_ROWS:
    tgt = tg[tg.drug.str.lower().apply(lambda s: any(k in s for k in keys))]
    genes = sorted(set(tgt.target_gene))
    rows.append(dict(dmt=name, rdkg=hit(rd_txt, keys), prokn_indication=hit(pk_txt, keys), prokn_target=bool(genes),
                     wikidata=hit(wd_txt, keys), target_genes=", ".join(genes) or "—",
                     target_tiers=", ".join(f"{g}:{m.set_index('symbol').tier.get(g, '–')}" for g in genes) or "—"))
dmt = pd.DataFrame(rows); dmt.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/dmt_kg_coverage.csv", index=False)
STATS["dmt_rows"] = len(dmt); STATS["dmt_all4"] = int(dmt[["rdkg", "prokn_indication", "prokn_target", "wikidata"]].all(axis=1).sum())
STATS["dmt_target_missing"] = ", ".join(dmt[~dmt.prokn_target].dmt)
pk = Q["prokn_indications"]
STATS.update({"prokn_compounds": len(pk), "prokn_phase4": int((pk.max_phase == 4).sum()), "prokn_phase3": int((pk.max_phase == 3).sum()),
              "prokn_targets_n": tg.target_gene.nunique(), "drug_names_total": len(dagg)})
# repurposing: prokn MS-trial drugs acting on tier A–C genes that are not approved MS DMTs
appr = {"daclizumab", "alemtuzumab", "ocrelizumab", "ofatumumab", "rituximab", "ublituximab", "natalizumab", "fingolimod", "siponimod",
        "ozanimod", "ponesimod", "dimethyl", "diroximel", "monomethyl", "teriflunomide", "cholecalciferol", "ergocalciferol", "mitoxantrone"}
tt = tg.merge(m[["symbol", "tier", "n_sources"]], left_on="target_gene", right_on="symbol", how="left")
rep = tt[tt.tier.isin(["A", "B", "C"]) & ~tt.drug.str.lower().apply(lambda s: any(a in s for a in appr))]
rep = (rep.groupby("drug").agg(targets=("target_gene", lambda s: ", ".join(sorted(set(s)))), best_tier=("tier", "min"),
                               max_phase=("max_phase", "max"), action=("action", "first")).reset_index()
          .sort_values(["best_tier", "max_phase"], ascending=[True, False]))
rep.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/repurposing_candidates.csv", index=False)
STATS["repurpose_n"] = len(rep)
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 8.5))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, width_ratios=[1.35, 1], height_ratios=[1, 1.1])
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 0]); ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1]); ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
cols = ["rdkg", "prokn_indication", "prokn_target", "wikidata"]
mat = dmt[cols].astype(float).values
ax1.imshow(mat, cmap="Oranges", vmin=0, vmax=1.5, aspect="auto")
ax1.set_xticks(range(4)); ax1.set_xticklabels(["rdkg\ntreats", "prokn\nindication", "prokn\ndrug→target", "wikidata\nP2176"])
ax1.set_yticks(range(len(dmt))); ax1.set_yticklabels(dmt.dmt)
for i in range(mat.shape[0]):
    for j in range(4):
        ax1.text(j, i, "✓" if mat[i, j] else "–", ha="center", va="center", color="white" if mat[i, j] else "#999", fontsize=10)
    ax1.text(3.65, i, dmt.target_tiers[i], va="center", fontsize=8.5)
ax1.set_xlim(-0.5, 6.6); ax1.text(3.65, -0.9, "target gene : tier", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
F.panel_title(ax1, "A", "Disease-modifying therapies across KGs")
ph = pk.max_phase.fillna(-1).value_counts().sort_index()
ax2.bar([("n/a" if p == -1 else f"{p:g}") for p in ph.index], ph.values, color="#E69F00")
for x, v in enumerate(ph.values):

§5.5 Clinical phenotypes and biomarkers¶

Which clinical features and biomarkers do the graphs attach to MS, curated (rdkg) versus observed together in EHR cohorts (oard-kg)?

In [57]:
# Figure 5 — clinical phenotypes (rdkg curated, oard-kg EHR co-occurrence) and biomarkers (biomarkerkg, wikidata)

cur["hpo"] = cur.x.map(A.tail)
oa = Q["oard"].copy()
cur = cur.merge(oa[["hpo", "max_lor", "max_pair"]], on="hpo", how="left")
cur.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/phenotypes_curated.csv", index=False)
oa["in_rdkg"] = oa.hpo.isin(cur.hpo)
oa.sort_values("max_lor", ascending=False).to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/phenotypes_oard.csv", index=False)

import re as _re
oa["neuro"] = oa.label.str.contains(NEURO, flags=_re.I)
STATS.update({"pheno_rdkg": len(cur), "pheno_rdkg_in_oard": int(cur.max_lor.notna().sum()), "pheno_oard": len(oa),
              "pheno_oard_neuro": int(oa.neuro.sum())})

              "bm_gene_analytes": len(analytes)})
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 8))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, width_ratios=[1, 1.1], height_ratios=[1, 1])

§5.6 Epidemiology — prevalence map¶

Where is MS most common? Map prevalence by country.

In [58]:

§5.6 Epidemiology — correlates and risk factors¶

Test the latitude gradient and whether it survives adjustment for national income, alongside the risk and protective factors the graphs record.

In [60]:
# Figure 7 — prevalence correlates (latitude, GDP, continent) and literature risk/protective factors (biohealth, rdkg)
from scipy.stats import spearmanr, kruskal
ls = A.latitude_stats(e)
STATS.update({"rho_lat": round(float(ls["rho_lat"]), 3), "p_lat": f"{ls['p_lat']:.1e}", "n_lat": ls["n_lat"],
              "rho_gdp": round(float(ls["rho_gdp"]), 3), "p_gdp": f"{ls['p_gdp']:.1e}", "n_gdp": ls["n_gdp"],
              "rho_lat_gdp": round(float(ls["rho_lat_given_gdp"]), 3), "p_lat_gdp": f"{ls['p_lat_given_gdp']:.1e}"})
mo = e.dropna(subset=["mort_per_100k"])
r_m, p_m = spearmanr(mo.prev_per_100k, mo.mort_per_100k)
STATS.update({"rho_mort": round(float(r_m), 3), "p_mort": f"{p_m:.1e}", "n_mort": len(mo)})
cont = e.dropna(subset=["continent"]).groupby("continent").prev_per_100k.agg(["median", "count"]).sort_values("median", ascending=False)
cont.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/prevalence_by_continent.csv")
kw = kruskal(*[gr.prev_per_100k.values for _, gr in e.dropna(subset=["continent"]).groupby("continent") if len(gr) > 2])
STATS.update({"kw_p": f"{kw.pvalue:.1e}", "cont_europe": round(float(cont.loc["Europe", "median"]), 1),
              "cont_africa": round(float(cont.loc["Africa", "median"]), 1)})
# risk / protective factors: biohealth (literature-derived SemMedDB-style predications) + rdkg contributes_to
RF = {"Viral infection (EBV, HHV-6, HERV-W, CMV, measles…)": r"virus|viral|herpes|retrovir|measles|rubella|mumps|picorna|coronav|morbilli|rhinovir|spumavir|HTLV|T-Cell Leukemia",
      "Tobacco smoke / nicotine": r"smok|tobacco|nicotine|cigarette",
      "Vitamin D / sunlight": r"vitamin d|calcitriol|cholecalciferol|ergocalciferol|cod liver",
      "Adiposity / body size / diet": r"adipos|body weight|body size|obes|diet|food|meat|milk|dairy|salt|sodium chloride|fruit|vegetable|soft drink|coffee|fish",
      "Physical activity": r"exercise|physical activ|fitness|walking|leisure",
      "Air pollution / chemicals / metals": r"pollut|pesticide|solvent|lead|mercury|bisphenol|rodenticide|irritant",
      "Sex / age / genetics": r"female|male|sex|gender|age$|genetic|genotype|haplotype|trait|proband",
      "Bacteria / microbes": r"bacteri|streptococc|pseudomonas|helicobacter|acinetobacter|mycobacter|spirochaet"}
br = Q["biohealth_risk"].copy()
rdx = Q["rdkg_edges"]; rdx = rdx[rdx.p.str.endswith("contributes_to")].drop_duplicates("xlabel")
br = pd.concat([br.assign(kg="biohealth"), pd.DataFrame({"pred": "contributes_to", "entity": rdx.xlabel, "kg": "rdkg"})])
import re as _re
br["factor"] = br.entity.map(lambda s: next((k for k, p in RF.items() if _re.search(p, str(s), _re.I)), "Other"))
br.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/risk_factors.csv", index=False)
rf = br[br.factor != "Other"].groupby(["factor", "pred"]).entity.nunique().unstack(fill_value=0)
rf = rf.loc[rf.sum(axis=1).sort_values().index]
STATS.update({"rf_entities": int(br.entity.nunique()), "rf_viral": int(rf.loc[[i for i in rf.index if i.startswith("Viral")]].sum(axis=1).iloc[0])})
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 9))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=[1, 1])
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0]); ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1]); ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :])
CC = {"Europe": "#0072B2", "Asia": "#E69F00", "Africa": "#009E73", "North America": "#D55E00", "South America": "#CC79A7",
      "Oceania": "#56B4E9", "Seven seas (open ocean)": "#999999"}
MK = {"Europe": "o", "Asia": "s", "Africa": "^", "North America": "D", "South America": "v", "Oceania": "P", "Seven seas (open ocean)": "X"}
for c_, gr in e.dropna(subset=["continent"]).groupby("continent"):
    ax1.scatter(gr.abs_lat, gr.prev_per_100k, s=28, c=CC.get(c_, "#999"), marker=MK.get(c_, "o"), label=c_, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4)
ax1.set_yscale("log"); ax1.set_xlabel("|latitude| of country centroid (wikidata P625), degrees"); ax1.set_ylabel("prevalence per 100,000 (log)")

         transform=ax1.transAxes, va="top", fontsize=8.5, bbox=dict(fc="white", ec="#ccc"))
F.legend_outside(ax1, where="right", title="continent")

§6.1 GO and Reactome enrichment¶

Do the signature genes share biology? Test GO biological processes and Reactome pathways for over-representation.

In [61]:

              "re_n": n_re, "re_N": int(Q["re_N"].N_reactome[0]), "re_tested": len(re_), "re_sig": int((re_.fdr < 0.05).sum()),
              "sig_in_prokn": int(Q["sig_n"].n_in_prokn[0])})
THEMES = {"Interferon / JAK-STAT": r"interferon|JAK|STAT|type I|type II", "T-cell activation / TCR": r"T cell|T-cell|TCR|CD28|PD-1|ZAP|co-stimul|Costimulation|alpha-beta",
          "B cell / antigen presentation": r"B cell|antigen|MHC|immunoglobulin|BCR", "Innate / inflammasome": r"inflamma|NLRP|Toll|TLR|innate|NK|natural killer|microglia|IL-1|Interleukin-1 ",
          "Cytokine signalling": r"cytokine|interleukin|Interleukin|IL-|chemokine|TNF|tumor necrosis"}
TCOL = {"Interferon / JAK-STAT": "#D55E00", "T-cell activation / TCR": "#0072B2", "B cell / antigen presentation": "#009E73",
        "Innate / inflammasome": "#CC79A7", "Cytokine signalling": "#E69F00", "Other": "#999999"}
import re as _re
def theme_of(lbl):
    for t, pat in THEMES.items():
        if _re.search(pat, lbl, _re.I):
            return t
    return "Other"
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 8.2))
for ax, d, letter, ttl in [(axes[0], go, "A", f"GO biological process (top 20 of {len(go)} tested)"),
                           (axes[1], re_, "B", f"Reactome pathways (top 20 of {len(re_)} tested)")]:
    t = d.head(20)
    labs = [l if len(l) <= 48 else l[:46] + "…" for l in t.label]
    th = [theme_of(l) for l in t.label]
    F.ranked_barh(ax, labs, list(-np.log10(t.fdr)), themes=th, theme_colors=TCOL,
                  annots=[f"×{f:.1f} ({k}/{K})" for f, k, K in zip(t.fold, t.k, t.K)], xlabel="−log10(FDR)")
    F.panel_title(ax, letter, ttl)
F.theme_legend(axes[1], {k: v for k, v in TCOL.items()}, where="below", title="theme")
F.finalize(fig, 8, "figures/fig8_enrichment.png")

§6.2 Protein-interaction network¶

How do the signature proteins interact, and which are the hubs?

In [62]:
# Figure 9 — protein–protein interaction network among the MS core signature (nestkg)
import networkx as nx
pe = A.ppi_edges(Q)
G = nx.Graph(); G.add_edges_from(zip(pe.gene_a, pe.gene_b))
tier_of = dict(zip(m.symbol, m.tier))
deg = dict(G.degree())
STATS.update({"ppi_edges": G.number_of_edges(), "ppi_nodes": G.number_of_nodes(),
              "ppi_hub1": max(deg, key=deg.get), "ppi_hub1_deg": max(deg.values())})
hubs = pd.DataFrame({"symbol": list(deg), "degree": list(deg.values())})
hubs["tier"] = hubs.symbol.map(tier_of).fillna("–")
hubs["betweenness"] = hubs.symbol.map(nx.betweenness_centrality(G))
hubs = hubs.sort_values("degree", ascending=False); hubs.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/ppi_hubs.csv", index=False)
core = [n for n in G if deg[n] >= 8]
H = G.subgraph(core).copy()
H = H.subgraph(max(nx.connected_components(H), key=len)).copy()
STATS["ppi_shown_nodes"] = H.number_of_nodes()
pos = nx.spring_layout(H, seed=7, k=0.55, iterations=200)
TC = {"A": "#D55E00", "B": "#E69F00", "C": "#56B4E9", "D": "#BBBBBB", "–": "#BBBBBB"}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 10))
nx.draw_networkx_edges(H, pos, ax=ax, alpha=0.12, width=0.6)
for t, shape in [("A", "o"), ("B", "s"), ("C", "^"), ("D", "D"), ("–", "D")]:
    nl = [n for n in H if tier_of.get(n, "–") == t]
    if nl:
        nx.draw_networkx_nodes(H, pos, nodelist=nl, node_shape=shape, node_color=TC[t], ax=ax,
                               node_size=[25 + 6 * deg[n] for n in nl], edgecolors="white", linewidths=0.5,
                               label=f"tier {t}" if t != "–" else "not tiered")
lab = sorted(H, key=lambda n: -deg[n])[:30]
nx.draw_networkx_labels(H, pos, labels={n: n for n in lab}, font_size=8.5, ax=ax,
                        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.15", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.75))
ax.axis("off")
F.legend_outside(ax, where="below", title="confidence tier (size ∝ degree)", ncol=5)
F.panel_title(ax, "", f"PPI network of MS core genes (degree ≥ 8; {H.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {H.number_of_edges()} edges)")
F.finalize(fig, 9, "figures/fig9_ppi_network.png")

§6.3 Mechanistic map¶

Tie it together: link MS to mechanistic modules, their best-supported genes, and the drugs that target them.

In [63]:
# Figure 10 — mechanistic map: MS → mechanistic module → tier A–C gene → drug (prokn drug→target edges only)
import tempfile
from mechanistic_map import render_mechanistic_map
MODULES = {
    "HLA class II / antigen presentation": ["HLA-DRB1", "HLA-DQB1", "HLA-DRA", "HLA-DPB1", "CD40", "CD86"],
    "T-cell activation & co-stimulation": ["IL2RA", "IL7R", "CD58", "CD6", "CBLB", "TAGAP", "PTPRC", "MALT1", "CD52", "DHODH"],
    "Cytokine / JAK–STAT / Th1–Th17": ["IFNG", "IL17A", "IL12A", "IL12B", "TYK2", "STAT3", "STAT4", "TNFRSF1A", "CSF2"],
    "B cell / plasma cell": ["MS4A1", "CD19", "CXCR5", "TNFSF13B", "IKZF3", "BTK"],
    "Innate / microglia / inflammasome": ["NLRP3", "IL1B", "TLR4", "ITGAM", "MERTK", "CASP1", "KIT", "CCR2"],
    "Lymphocyte trafficking / BBB": ["ITGA4", "S1PR1", "S1PR5"],
    "Redox / remyelination / conduction": ["KEAP1", "LINGO1", "RGMA", "HRH1", "KCNA1", "VDR"],
}
genes_in_kg = set(m.symbol)
assert all(g in genes_in_kg for v in MODULES.values() for g in v), [g for v in MODULES.values() for g in v if g not in genes_in_kg]
drug_short = lambda d: d.replace(" Fumaric Acid", "").replace(" Hydrochloride", "").replace(" Lauryl Sulfate", "").replace(" Fumarate", "") if "Dimethyl" not in d and "Diroximel" not in d and "Monomethyl" not in d else d
DRUGS = {}
for mod, gl in MODULES.items():
    d = tg[tg.target_gene.isin(gl) & (tg.max_phase.fillna(0) >= 2)].copy()
    d["short"] = d.drug.map(drug_short)
    d = d.sort_values(["max_phase", "short"], ascending=[False, True]).drop_duplicates("short")
    DRUGS[mod] = d.short.head(8).tolist()
mod_rows = [(mod, g, m.set_index("symbol").tier.get(g), "; ".join(sorted(set(tg[tg.target_gene == g].drug))))
            for mod, gl in MODULES.items() for g in gl]
pd.DataFrame(mod_rows, columns=["module", "gene", "tier", "prokn_drugs"]).to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/mechanistic_modules.csv", index=False)
STATS["mech_modules"] = len(MODULES); STATS["mech_genes"] = sum(len(v) for v in MODULES.values())
STATS["mech_drugs"] = len({d for v in DRUGS.values() for d in v})
tmp_png = render_mechanistic_map("Multiple sclerosis", MODULES, DRUGS, out_path=os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "ms_mechanistic_map_raw.png"),
                       title="MS gene–module–drug mechanistic map (entities retrieved from OKN KGs)",
                       subtitle="modules = analyst grouping of tier A–C genes guided by GO/Reactome enrichment; drugs = prokn drug→target, max phase ≥ 2",
                       gene_legend="Gene (tier A–C or drug target)", drug_legend="Drug (prokn, phase ≥ 2)")
img = plt.imread(tmp_png)  # place the rendered network on a report-style figure and save it
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(img.shape[1] / 150, img.shape[0] / 150))
ax.imshow(img); ax.axis("off")
F.finalize(fig, 10, "figures/fig10_mechanistic_map.png")

Summary quantities (stats.json) and ranked-results extract¶

Collect the headline numbers in stats.json, which fills the report's numbers, so the prose cannot drift from the computation, and write the ranked-results table.

pig = A.digcfdekg_table(Q).sort_values("pigean", ascending=False)

STATS["n_pigean_ge3"] = int((pig.pigean >= 3).sum())
cols = ["symbol", "entrez", "tier", "score", "n_sources", "sources", "spoke_okn", "rdkg", "digcfdekg", "pigean_score", "wikidata",
        "biomarkerkg", "gxa_up", "gxa_down", "gxa_ifn_response", "prokn_drug_target", "drugs", "max_drug_phase", "ppi_degree_core", "ncRNA"]
ranked = m[cols].copy(); ranked["sources"] = ranked.sources.map(lambda l: "; ".join(l)); ranked.insert(0, "rank", range(1, len(ranked) + 1))
ranked.to_csv(f"{EXTRACTS}/ranked_results.csv", index=False)
json.dump(STATS, open(f"{EXTRACTS}/stats.json", "w"), indent=1, default=str)

{'tier_A': 55, 'tier_B': 107, 'go_sig': 159, 're_sig': 58, 'rho_lat': 0.836, 'top10': 'IL2RA, IFNG, CD86, CD6, IL17A, CD58, IL7R, TNFRSF1A, MERTK, TAGAP'}

Conclusions¶

Summary of findings

  • Evidence. 1,748 genes have MS evidence in at least one graph; 55 reach tier A and 107 tier B. The top-ranked genes are IL2RA, IFNG, CD86, CD6 and IL17A.
  • Biology. The signature is overwhelmingly immune: 159 of 167 GO BP terms and 58 of 60 Reactome pathways pass FDR < 0.05, and IFNG is the main interaction hub (degree 112 among 178 core genes).
  • Expression. Disease expression is noisy: 11 genes recur across four MS-vs-control contrasts and 3 change in the same direction, while IFN-β treatment gives a robust interferon response.
  • Therapeutics. prokn records 204 MS-indicated compounds acting on 71 target genes, but only IL2RA, IL17A, IL12A and VDR have tier-A genetic support, and IFN-β, glatiramer and cladribine have no drug→target edge.
  • Epidemiology. Prevalence ranges from 1.29 to 216.5 per 100,000 across 200 countries and rises with latitude (ρ = 0.836), still 0.743 after adjusting for GDP.

Answer. Seen through the federation, MS is a polygenic disorder of adaptive immunity anchored on HLA class II, with an innate and microglial arm. Its therapies mostly act on lymphocyte trafficking, depletion and redox rather than on the top genetic genes, and its prevalence follows latitude independently of income. The graphs also have clear gaps and errors: no CIS term, a retained PRMS term, no NfL in biomarkerkg, and viral "causes" edges in biohealth.

Main limitation. Every relationship here is associative (curated, genetic, text-mined or EHR co-occurrence), and the epidemiology is ecological at country level, so nothing supports causal or clinical inference. Full limitations are in the report.
